profile.documented: A vision and text chat model with a documented context limit of 131072 tokens and broad language coverage. It is run with greedy sampling and a documented prompt adapter that uses short task prefixes such as Text Recognition and Table Recognition. Its documented scenario is transcription-style parsing and information extraction, not general question answering.
profile.role_in_run: HOME-23, OCR transcription, was designed around this model. That test measures transcription of text images and extraction of table grids from document images.

overall.rating_basis: Mean semantic quality 0.945 over 1 scored test, home-test quality 0.945, and an OK rate of 0.188. The rating rests on a single test and is weakly supported.

home_test.title: OCR transcription
home_test.analysis: Transcription quality is high: mean semantic quality 0.945 across all 16 cases, with 3 fully accepted and most of the rest scoring above 0.8. The gap between semantic quality and strict quality comes from two behaviors: the model repeats the transcribed sentence after itself, which breaks the exact-output contract, and table transcriptions run past the token limit so the run is cut off even though the captured cells are correct. The practical reading is that the model reads accurately but its output control is weak: repetition on plain text and over-long output on tables.

strengths: Transcribes English and German prose images with zero character errors, as shown by the exact matches on 3 of 16 cases.
Captures table grids with perfect cell-level scores on all 6 table cases, including multi-column layouts.
Holds a 0.945 mean semantic quality across the full 16-case set, the highest single-test mean in this group.
weaknesses: Repeats transcribed sentences, which breaks exact-output matching even when every character is right.
Table outputs overflow the token budget, so 6 of 6 table cases were cut off before finishing.
Non-English transcriptions outside German degrade, with script mixing and dropped words on 3 cases.
use_when: English document-page transcription where a light de-duplication pass can clean repeated sentences (HOME-23).
Table-grid capture from invoice or report images where cell content matters more than exact output length (HOME-23).
German-language prose transcription, which matched exactly in this run (HOME-23).
avoid_when: Strict exact-output pipelines with no post-processing, since repetition triggers format penalties.
Long-table capture under tight token budgets, where output will be cut off mid-table.
Mixed-script archival OCR without review, where character substitutions slip through.
hardware_fit: Cold load takes about 2.7 seconds and generation runs near 254 tokens per second, the fastest in this group, so interactive OCR feels immediate. The measurements show full accelerator offload with no partial CPU fallback, which keeps that speed consistent. The practical consequence is that this model is cheap to keep resident and fast per page on this hardware.
bottom_line: The strongest transcriber in this group with a 0.945 mean on its own OCR test, held back only by output discipline rather than reading ability. Repetition and over-long tables are fixable with post-processing and larger token budgets. For pure image-to-text work on this hardware it is the practical choice.

home_test.title: Bug repair with hidden tests and bug-line localisation
home_test.analysis: The model fixes code well but formats it badly: semantic quality 0.875 with most hidden-test suites passing, yet strict quality 0.0 because all 12 answers wrapped the code in prose and fences. The bug-line report is systematically off by one in 5 cases, for example reporting line 4 where the reference says line 3. The reading is that repair skill is real and localisation is close but consistently shifted, while output-contract compliance is entirely absent.

failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: It prepended phrases like introductory sentences and wrapped solutions in fenced blocks on both the bug-repair and code-generation tests, even when all hidden tests passed.
failure_analysis.why_it_matters: Any pipeline that extracts raw code without stripping prose will mis-handle every answer from this model.

failure_analysis.what_the_model_did: It introduced queries with sentences describing the question and wrapped them in fences instead of returning the bare statement.

failure_analysis.why_it_matters: Direct execution of its answers fails unless a stripping step removes the prose first.

strengths: Repairs buggy functions effectively, passing full hidden-test suites while scoring 0.875 on its home repair test.
Generates new code from specifications at 0.806 with 15 of 16 answers functionally close.
Writes working SQL with 4 exact matches and a 0.786 mean over the scored query cases.
weaknesses: Never complies with output-only contracts: all 40 scored answers carried extra prose, leaving strict quality at 0.
Reports bug lines off by one in 5 of 12 repair cases, a systematic shift rather than random error.
Loses coverage to slow generation, with 8 SQL cases never run before the deadline.
use_when: Bug-fixing assistance where a developer reads the answer and hidden tests verify it (HOME-06).
First-draft code generation from a written specification with tests run afterward (HOME-14).
SQL drafting for retail and HR style queries where results are checked before use (HOME-20).
avoid_when: Strict machine-parsed code output with no stripping step, since every answer adds prose.
Automated bug localisation without review, given the consistent off-by-one line shift.
Tight-deadline batch SQL jobs, where 8 of 20 cases never finished in this run.
hardware_fit: Cold load takes about 3.4 seconds with first-token latency near 0.27 seconds and generation near 76 tokens per second. The measurements show full accelerator offload, so it runs entirely on the graphics card. The practical consequence is steady but unhurried generation: fine for single repairs, slow for large batch jobs on this hardware.
bottom_line: A genuinely capable code model rated 6.9 whose 0.822 mean reflects real repair and generation skill masked by zero format compliance. With a prose-stripping step and a minus-one line correction it becomes practical. Without those two wrappers its answers cannot be consumed automatically.

Format handling improved under the adapter but comprehension did not, so this is a genuine extraction-capability limit of the compact model rather than a contract artifact.

profile.documented: A text chat model with tool and structured-output capabilities, a documented context limit of 128000 tokens, and documented support for English plus nine other languages. It always reasons internally, with a documented quirk that disabling reasoning leaks thinking text into the answer. Its vendor note discourages it for heavy programming work.
profile.role_in_run: HOME-21, long tool chains, was designed around this model. That test measures multi-step tool calling over up to 8 turns to complete chained tasks.

overall.rating_basis: Mean semantic quality 0.674 over 15 scored tests, home-test quality 0.375, and an OK rate of 0.695. Breadth is the strength and the home tool test is the weak spot.

home_test.title: Long tool chains
home_test.analysis: The home tool test is weak at 0.375 with only 2 of 8 chains completed: 5 answers contained no parseable tool call at all and the rest picked wrong states. This is the model's worst tool result even though single-turn calling elsewhere is perfect, which points to multi-turn state tracking rather than call formatting as the failure. For chained tool work this model cannot be trusted without an external state check.

strengths: Solves multi-step word problems perfectly with 20 of 20 numeric answers correct.
Handles single-turn function calling perfectly with all 30 calls correct.
Answers grounded RAG questions at 0.938 and competition math at 0.917, showing solid reasoning with retrieval.
weaknesses: Fails long tool chains at 0.375 on its own home test, with 5 of 8 turns coming back empty.
Gets cut off while reasoning on 13 cases, delivering no answer on long-context and optimization tasks.
Produces field-level value errors on 21 classification and extraction cases despite valid formatting.
use_when: Single-turn function calling where every call in this run was correct (HOME-24).
Math word problems with numeric answers, solved perfectly here (HOME-13).
Grounded question answering with citations, where it matched on 15 of 16 cases (HOME-03).
avoid_when: Multi-turn tool chains without an external state check, given the 0.375 home-test result (HOME-21).
Long-context questions under tight token budgets, where reasoning consumes the budget with no answer (HOME-09, HOME-10).
Unreviewed classification output, where wrong field values hide inside valid-looking objects (HOME-01, HOME-12).
hardware_fit: Cold load takes about 4.0 seconds with first-token latency near 0.10 seconds and generation near 220 tokens per second, among the fastest text models here. The measurements show full accelerator offload, so it stays on the graphics card. The practical consequence is snappy interactive use, though its always-on reasoning still fills token budgets quickly on long tasks.
bottom_line: A broad and fast generalist rated 5.9 with 15 scored tests, perfect on single-turn calls and word problems but weak on the multi-turn chaining it was built for. Use it for single-step reasoning and calling tasks. Keep it away from long chains and long-context work without guardrails.

For a safety gate that asymmetry matters: it never over-blocks safe content but lets two unsafe cases through.

profile.documented: A text chat model with tool and structured-output capabilities, a documented context limit of 131072 tokens, and documented support for English and seven other languages. It is run with greedy sampling and packaged stop sequences. Its broad capabilities span classification, retrieval-style QA, extraction, reasoning, code, routing, SQL, and function calling.
profile.role_in_run: HOME-09, long-context wiki QA, was designed around this model. That test measures answering questions from long wiki-style documents with a short answer plus quoted evidence sections.

This is the only perfect long-context score in the group and shows the model can hold a 20K-token document and cite exact sections. For long-document QA it is the demonstrated reference in this run.

strengths: Answers long-document questions perfectly at 1.0 with correct evidence on all 8 home cases.
Extracts templates perfectly at 1.0 with all 12 cases exactly matched.
Repairs bugs at 0.972 and converts HTML at 0.888, showing strong code and document skills.
weaknesses: Scores 0.0 on competition math and constrained optimization, with wrong values and broken constraints.
Makes spurious function calls on 11 single-turn cases, its largest single failure pattern.
Tracks multilingual log states poorly at 0.042 and chains long tools weakly at 0.4.
use_when: Long-document question answering with evidence citations, perfect here (HOME-09).
Template extraction from long texts, perfect on all 12 cases (HOME-12).
Bug repair with hidden-test verification afterward, near-perfect at 0.972 (HOME-06).
avoid_when: Competition math and constrained optimization, both scored 0.0 (HOME-04, HOME-17).
Single-turn function calling without call validation, given 11 spurious calls (HOME-24).
Multilingual log state tracking, which failed at 0.042 (HOME-10).
hardware_fit: Cold load takes about 4.1 seconds with first-token latency near 0.19 seconds and generation near 77 tokens per second. The measurements show full accelerator offload, so it stays on the graphics card. The practical consequence is deliberate pacing: excellent for quality-first document work, less suited to high-throughput batch jobs on this hardware.
bottom_line: The broadest model in this group with 17 scored tests and a 7.7 rating, perfect on its long-document home test and extraction, but unreliable on math, optimization, and strict single-turn calling. Give it document, extraction, and repair work with validation on code. Keep it away from math and optimization.
